criticResolutions: Following spec §5.4 (the plan's Join/Request clubs step would show one club with a dead button): B12-social builds step 5 follow-first. Every row gets Follow → Following ✓ through POST/DELETE /api/orgs/[slug]/follow with source=onboarding. SAE is listed and followable. audience_blocked clubs stay listed. Invited rows pin to the top with Accept. The rule set is in clubRowView and B13 mirrors it.

Founder decision 'open clubs show Follow AND Join together' overrides §5.4's 'Never Join on this step': only join_state can_join rows add an outline Join. can_request, invite_only and audience_blocked rows show Follow only.

C8 (the org-level follow_state collides with UserCard's person follow_state): the field is read in one place, isFollowingOrg(), which accepts follow_state==='following' or viewer_follows===true. The F2 contract can rename without touching the UI.

C9 (the copy table has no row for hidden clubs): discover never returns hidden clubs (api/orgs/route.ts:353), and a POST follow 404 removes the row with 'This club isn't available anymore.' No hidden branch is needed on onboarding.
C13 and C27 (a count of 1 identifies the person; a failed read shows as 0): onboarding rows show NO member or follower counts (clubRowView meta has none).

C14 and the founder decision (officers can see who follows a club, and students are told): every non-open club row that isn't joined or invited carries the sub-line 'Officers can see who follows this club.'
C16 (Join hidden behind Follow): resolved as above. Join sits beside Follow on open clubs and is never gated on following.

C17 ('nothing here can 403' is false): the clubs step handles 403 terms_required (toast with the Review Terms action via vibeRequest), 404 (row removed), 409 member_follows (row locks) and 429 (mapped toast). No copy claims a follow can't fail.
C7 (leaving a join-created follow): nothing on onboarding leaves a club. A member row renders a locked 'Following ✓' with 'Members follow automatically', which matches the 409 member_follows rule.
